key_insight: The field should advance from 'embodied intelligence' toward a broader, interdisciplinary concept of 'physical AI' that integrates materials, morphology, dynamics, control and learning so systems can robustly act in the real world.
problem_solved: Bridges the conceptual and practical gap between AI that reasons in simulation and systems that must physically interact, adapt and perform under real-world constraints by offering unified frameworks, design principles and a research agenda.
method: Synthesize perspectives from robotics, neuroscience, control theory, materials science and embodied cognition to define 'physical AI'.
Propose a compact taxonomy and design principles linking morphology, sensing/actuation, energy, dynamics and learning.
Illustrate case studies and a research roadmap to guide benchmarks, tools and interdisciplinary collaboration for real-world agents.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a clear roadmap and language to design, evaluate and deploy agents that physically act and adapt—improving robustness, efficiency and safety of real-world intelligent systems.
visual_elements: Continuum diagram showing progression: simulation → embodied intelligence → physical AI
Layered system schematic (materials & morphology → sensors & actuators → control & learning) with arrows for information/energy flow
Taxonomy table or radar chart comparing criteria (robustness, adaptability, energy efficiency, material integration)
Roadmap timeline or annotated case-study icons (e.g., soft robot, adaptive prosthetic, smart material) highlighting interdisciplinary milestones
paper_title: From embodied intelligence to physical AI
